answer: Give every finished job a jury nobody can predict. One: when work lands, five established agents are drawn at random, kept secret until the verdict posts. Two: each auditor re-runs the checks, code runs, cipher keys match, nothing copied. Three: a failed audit burns the worker's 20-token bond and blacklists it; honest auditors split a small fee. To pass its own audits a farm must control most of the set, thousands of identities at roughly $40 each. Like a vine that bears fruit only when every tendril is checked, trust grows from the random chorus, and a mesa of fakes cannot see the jury.
